mission.title: Install and Configure Docker Desktop Kubernetes
mission.description: Docker Desktop for Mac provides an integrated Docker experience on macOS, including a local Kubernetes cluster. It's ideal for developers looking to test and develop applications in a Kubernetes environment without the overhead of managing a full cluster. However, it may not be suitable for production workloads due to resource limitations and lack of advanced features.

steps.title: Download Docker Desktop
steps.description:
This step installs Docker Desktop, which includes Kubernetes support.

```bash

open https://store.docker.com/editions/community/docker-ce-desktop-mac

```

> This opens the Docker Desktop download page.

steps.title: Install Docker Desktop
steps.description:
Run the downloaded installer to set up Docker Desktop on your Mac.

```bash

open ~/Downloads/Docker.dmg

sudo cp -R /Volumes/Docker/Docker.app /Applications/

hdiutil unmount /Volumes/Docker

```

> Replace 'Docker.dmg' with the actual filename if different.
> This copies Docker Desktop to your Applications folder.
> This unmounts the Docker disk image.

steps.title: Start Docker Desktop and Enable Kubernetes
steps.description:
Launch Docker Desktop and enable the Kubernetes feature in settings.

```bash

open -a Docker

sleep 10 && open -a 'Docker' --args --enable-kubernetes

```

> This starts Docker Desktop.
> Wait for Docker to start and enable Kubernetes.

steps.title: Verify Kubernetes Installation
steps.description:
Check if Kubernetes is running correctly on Docker Desktop.

```bash

kubectl cluster-info

kubectl get nodes

```

> This command displays information about the Kubernetes cluster.
> This command lists the nodes in the cluster.

uninstall.title: Uninstall Docker Desktop
uninstall.description:
This will quit Docker Desktop, move the application to the Trash, and remind you to review any leftover Docker settings.

```bash

osascript -e 'quit app "Docker"'

osascript -e 'tell application "Finder" to delete POSIX file "/Applications/Docker.app"'

echo "Review ~/.docker and remove it manually if you no longer need the Docker settings."

```

> This quits Docker Desktop.
> This moves Docker Desktop from Applications to the Trash.
> This reminds you to review the Docker configuration directory before deleting it.
commands: osascript -e 'tell application "Finder" to delete POSIX file "/Applications/Docker.app"'
echo "Review ~/.docker and remove it manually if you no longer need the Docker settings."

upgrade.title: Upgrade Docker Desktop
upgrade.description:
Backup your Docker settings, perform the upgrade, and verify the installation.

```bash

cp -r ~/.docker ~/.docker_backup

open https://store.docker.com/editions/community/docker-ce-desktop-mac

open ~/Downloads/Docker.dmg

sudo cp -R /Volumes/Docker/Docker.app /Applications/

open -a Docker

kubectl get nodes

```

> This creates a backup of your Docker settings.
> Download the latest version from the Docker website.
> Open the downloaded Docker installer.
> Replace the existing Docker app with the new version.
> Start Docker Desktop after the upgrade.
> Verify that Kubernetes is still running after the upgrade.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Kubernetes is not running'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** Docker Desktop may not have started properly or Kubernetes is not enabled.

**Fix:**
Restart Docker Desktop and ensure Kubernetes is enabled in settings.

troubleshooting.title: kubectl: command not found
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** kubectl is not installed or not in the PATH.

**Fix:**
Ensure Docker Desktop is installed and running, which includes kubectl.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Unable to connect to the server: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:6443: connect: connection refused'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** Kubernetes API server is not running.

**Fix:**
Check Docker Desktop settings to ensure Kubernetes is enabled and restart Docker.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'context deadline exceeded'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** Kubernetes may be taking too long to start or is in a crash loop.

**Fix:**
Restart Docker Desktop and check the logs for errors.

resolution.summary: You should see output similar to 'Kubernetes master is running at https://127.0.0.1:6443' and a list of nodes when running 'kubectl get nodes'.
